answer: A new agent's first payout must extend a signed artifact from an established one: the hash of that predecessor's output seeds the next task, so answers cannot be precomputed. A ripple of one honest result runs down every branch, and a fork that skips a link fails the check. A thousand clones from one rack queue behind the same predecessor, each re-deriving a round of dependent labor, so an extra identity costs a full round of work rather than a keypress. A falcon stoops along one line of flight, not at the flock; a hollow account has nothing to chain onto and starves at the gate.
